audit_result.proof_trace: The function performs a non-atomic read-modify-write: it reads the latest attendance type (L42-44) without a FOR UPDATE lock, then computes the toggle, then inserts (L49-50) — all under PostgreSQL's default READ COMMITTED isolation with no serialization guard. Two concurrent calls for the same card_id will both read the same v_last_type before either INSERT is visible, causing both to write the same new_type (e.g., two consecutive 'in' records). No unique constraint or ON CONFLICT clause prevents the duplicate insert.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An attacker (or physical double-tap within the NFC scan window) fires two simultaneous anonymous RPC calls to `attendance.record_attendance_by_card` for the same card_id; both read v_last_type='out', both compute v_new_type='in', and both INSERT, producing duplicate attendance records that corrupt the clock-in/clock-out state for the victim user.

PROP-e5782b58-pre-004.text: Record_attendance_by_card RPC must be atomic to prevent race conditions on concurrent punches.
PROP-e5782b58-pre-004.assertion: forall concurrent calls record_attendance(card_id): serializable isolation on (user_id, date) pair
